content.overview: BNS s. 323 — Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property. BNS restatement of IPC 424. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 424. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 323 is the rule on “Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property”. The section provides that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently conceals or removes any property of himself or any other person, or dishonestly or fraudulently assists in the concealment or removal thereof, or dishonestly releases any demand or claim to which he is entitled, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years , or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 323 exists so that “Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.
